title: Wu et al. (2025), Evaluating indoor thermal resilience of passive and low-power cooling shelters for outdoor workers in India
method: EnergyPlus/OpenStudio comparison of passive and low-power packages; modeled WBGT and extended heat index.
findings: Ventilation and fans were prominent interventions in the modeled comparisons.
limitations: Not a measured SAAYA result. Airflow effects use study-specific relationships; climate and geometry differ from Vellore.
decision: Test simple shade, roof and airflow first; do not import modeled temperature reductions into product claims.

title: WHO/WMO (2025), Climate change and workplace heat stress: technical report and guidance
status: Official publication overview inspected; report PDF not fully reviewed
method: Evidence-based occupational guidance, not a shelter experiment.
findings: Supports tailored heat action programmes and coordinated prevention.
limitations: Overview does not provide a design certification or SAAYA performance data.
decision: Provide water, rest and assistance features within an occupational programme; never issue a personal safe status.

title: Santamouris & Vasilakopoulou (2026), Passive cooling for the built environment
status: Publisher metadata verified; full text inaccessible in this review
method: Review; detailed extraction pending full-text access.
scale: Nature Reviews Clean Technology 2,571–587; published 2 July 2026.
findings: Publisher record confirms the review; quantitative findings were not extracted.
limitations: Do not treat the dossier synopsis as independently verified detailed evidence.
decision: Background reading; no numeric design requirement derived from inaccessible text.

title: Binarti & Kubota (2026), A Review of Passive-Cooling Techniques for Buildings in Hot–Humid Climate Zones
status: Publisher metadata/search excerpt verified; full text blocked (429)
method: Review; extraction limited to publisher listing.
scale: Buildings 16(12),2288; publisher listing dates it 6 June 2026.
findings: Publisher excerpt concerns thermal stress and dependence on air conditioning.
limitations: Study selection, full conclusions and quantitative comparisons remain unverified.
decision: Keep humidity sensitivity as a test requirement; do not attribute unverified savings to this review.

title: Du, Wu & Miao (2026), Passive radiative cooling materials for extreme weather: mechanisms, design strategies, and application advances
status: Metadata and abstract verified; full-text retrieval intermittent
method: Materials review, not a SAAYA field trial.
findings: Practical radiative cooling is constrained by humidity, soiling, aging and moisture.
limitations: No tested low-cost coating specification or Vellore lifetime established here.
decision: Begin with a serviceable reflective roof; log cleaning and retest dirty/aged samples before premium materials.

title: Soleimani, Dehghan & Dehghan (2026), Effect of vest structure, airflow velocity, and humidity on evaporative cooling capacity using a thermal manikin
method: Four vest designs tested on a heated torso manikin; energy, evaporation and thermal images measured in two-hour trials.
findings: Air speed, humidity and vest construction affected cooling and water-use efficiency.
limitations: Garments on a manikin are not an open shelter or human recovery trial. Abstract contains a30°C mention despite35/40°C methods; no peak numeric claim reused.
decision: Measure actual air speed and water consumption if later testing evaporation; no vest-to-shelter performance transfer.

title: A comparative climate-based assessment of passive cooling strategies in buildings (2026)
status: Publisher abstract verified; full text inaccessible
method: Structured comparative review of124 studies across five climate zones.
findings: The abstract frames performance as climate dependent.
limitations: No full-text comparison tables or source-study quality audit completed.
decision: Compare local seasonal conditions; do not average reported cooling gains across climates.

title: WHO (2025), Workplace heat stress: questions and answers
findings: Heat stress combines environmental exposure, metabolic heat and clothing.
limitations: Air temperature and humidity cannot describe all individual exposure factors.
decision: No biometric diagnosis; assistance and human response remain independent of sensor conclusions.

title: Nejat et al. (2021), Passive cooling and natural ventilation by the windcatcher (Badgir)
method: Experimental and simulation study of windcatcher and upper wing wall.
climate: Wind-dependent; exact test climate not extracted.
findings: Investigates indoor air quality, comfort and passive cooling under different winds.
limitations: Full methods not inspected; cannot size SAAYA from title or historical precedent.
decision: High-level outlet is a testable option; use a removable wind scoop and measure directional performance.

title: Chaudhary & Sharmin (2026), Evaluating the Impact of Jaali Façades on Building Energy Demand in Jaipur’s Hot Semi-Arid Climate
status: Publisher methods and results inspected; simulation
method: DesignBuilder/EnergyPlus parametric comparison of perforation, depth, thickness and orientation.
scale: Air-conditioned office;84 simulations including three baselines.
findings: Screen geometry changes shading and modeled cooling demand.
limitations: Glazed office energy results do not establish ventilation benefits in a small open shelter.
decision: Interchangeable screens; compare shade coverage and pressure/airflow loss rather than copy the office optimum.

title: Experimental study of natural materials for an evaporative cooling design in hot-arid climate
method: Experimental natural-material cooling design with wetted clay elements.
findings: Evaporation through wetted clay cools and humidifies passing air.
limitations: Water hygiene, humidity and scale limit transfer; full results not reviewed.
decision: Removable separate non-potable experiment only; exclude from core Vellore prototype.

title: IMD Climatological Tables1991–2020:Vellore station43303
status: Official indexed station table inspected; complete PDF retrieval timed out
findings: Indexed wind table shows seasonal wind-direction changes and substantial calm periods.
limitations: Full temperature,humidity,rainfall rows not verified directly; no numeric climate design series published here. Normals do not replace site observations.
decision: Do not rely solely on a windcatcher; collect local seasonal T/RH,wind and rainfall before full-size sizing.

title: Penn:Carbon Neutral Solar Powered Outdoor Cooling Shelter
method: Design/project prior art, not independently replicated efficacy evidence.
findings: Solar-powered cooling shelter architecture predates this proposal.
limitations: Project performance and carbon claims are its own; not adopted as SAAYA results.
decision: Novelty candidate is transparent intervention verification, not combining a shelter with solar power.
